subject: Ω-LIN-T
definition: OAKBench for local linearization that records the approximation point, Jacobian or local operator, residual, validity domain, baseline, and reproducible numerical result.

claims.text: A local linear model can approximate a nonlinear system within an explicitly measured validity domain when its residual remains below a declared tolerance.
claims.canonical_key: local linear model is valid within measured residual domain
assumptions: the nonlinear map is differentiable in the tested neighborhood
the residual metric matches the intended downstream use
sampling covers the declared local domain
failure_conditions: the residual exceeds tolerance inside the claimed validity domain
the estimated domain changes materially under denser sampling
a simpler baseline yields equal or lower error with lower complexity

evidence.title: First-order local linear approximation and residual definition

metadata.model: f(x0 + delta) approximately f(x0) + J(x0) delta

evidence.title: Constant and direct nonlinear evaluation baselines

metadata.boundary: Demonstrates the benchmark machinery, not universal superiority of linearization.

transitions.cause: Local model, residual, and validity-domain contract were documented.
residues: benchmark coverage limited to selected examples

transitions.cause: Executable OAKBench and deterministic tests were added.
residues: broader nonlinear families and noise studies missing

transitions.cause: The implementation produced a reproducible residual and validity-domain report against baselines.
residues: independent reproduction and external benchmark suite missing

risks: local model extrapolated beyond validity domain
residual metric mismatched to downstream use
next_actions: Add nonlinear systems with known Taylor remainder bounds.
Publish a machine-readable validity-domain report with uncertainty fields.

metadata.oak_boundary: Demonstrated locally; not a universal theorem about all nonlinear systems.
